rows.audit_evidence: Swift ChapterTranslationRecord.lookupKey joins exactly bookFingerprintKey, unitStorageKey, targetLanguage, and promptVersion with '|' at vreader/Models/ChapterTranslationRecord.swift:93-104. Kotlin implements the same four-field rule in android/identity/src/main/kotlin/vreader/contracts/Identity.kt:52-61 and tests contracts/vectors/cache-key.json in IdentityConformanceTest.kt:146-161.

Swift declares schema version 3 in vreader/Services/Backup/BackupSectionDTOs.swift:17 and encodes sorted-key section envelopes in BackupDataCollector.swift:301-307. Kotlin mirrors section envelopes under android/identity/.../backup, configures omitted nulls and defaults in BackupJson.kt:60-73, and exercises the shared backup-sections vector in BackupConformanceTest.kt. The conformance comparison is semantic JSON equality, so the contract's 'stable key order' wording is stronger than what interoperability actually tests.

iOS preserves converted-EPUB local identity while persisting sourceCanonicalKey for converted Kindle imports: vreader/Services/BookImporter.swift:162-202 and vreader/Models/Book.swift:57-65. Android hashes the imported source stream directly and maps azw/azw3/mobi/prc to azw3 at android/identity/src/main/kotlin/vreader/contracts/DocumentFingerprint.kt:35-67. This matches the decision's source-byte cross-platform identity plus iOS-local converted artifact seam.

NFC and sorted canonical fields agree: Swift normalizes at vreader/Models/Locator.swift:116-140,183-185; Kotlin normalizes in android/identity/src/main/kotlin/vreader/contracts/Identity.kt:116. Validation rejects non-finite values on both sides. However, direct Swift canonicalJSON() silently omits non-finite progression values at Locator.swift:128-136, while Kotlin CanonicalLocator.canonicalJson throws via require at Identity.kt:90-91. The contract explicitly requires rejection rather than omission, so the public canonicalization behavior diverges.

Swift validates 64-character lowercase hex and non-negative byte count at vreader/Models/DocumentFingerprint.swift:29-45 and composes format:sha:size at lines 23-27. Kotlin hashes to lowercase hex and composes the same key at android/identity/src/main/kotlin/vreader/contracts/DocumentFingerprint.kt:23-48. Kindle extensions canonicalize to azw3 at lines 59-66; iOS's sourceCanonicalKey seam is implemented in BookImporter.swift:162-202.

This is the contract index/governance surface rather than an independently implementable wire format. Its referenced fingerprint, locator, cache-key, and backup surfaces all have Swift and Kotlin implementations and shared vectors.

The conformance lane is implemented by contracts/conformance/run.sh, Swift tests under vreaderTests/Contracts, and Kotlin tests under android/identity/src/test/kotlin/vreader/contracts. It is a test-orchestration contract, not a runtime serialization implementation.
